extracted.intended_audience: authors, creators, and publishing industry professionals seeking literary representation
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for authors preparing submissions and building relationships with a full-service literary agency (Folio) — from query polish and agent research to subrights, contracts, and long-term career strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency credibility / track record
rubrics_metrics.description: Folio has a visible track record: roster includes award winners, literary estates, and bestselling authors, opening doors at major publishers and helping projects get faster sales.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing notable sales, awards, and multi-territory deals on agent bios makes it easy to verify credibility and deal types, giving authors instant transparency. Editors know Folio’s agents and trust their vetting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent specialization matching
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents have specialties—fiction, nonfiction, children’s, YA, commercial, and upmarket—so you’ll connect with someone who understands your genre and market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research agent bios and pick those with matching specialties and recent relevant sales; matching multiplies chances of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial feedback quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents deliver real editorial feedback—line edits, pitch polish, and structure notes that significantly improve your manuscript’s marketability before it ever lands with an acquiring editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect thorough editorial rounds post-signing; clients who revise and listen outperform those who skip feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript readiness (polished work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a polished query letter with a completed manuscript (or proposal for nonfiction). Finish and revise your draft (or nonfiction proposal) until it shines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-assess: do you have a polished manuscript, competitive comps, and market knowledge? Weak or unfocused pitches rarely succeed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Query letter quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a polished query letter with a striking pitch, short author bio, clear comps, and a completed manuscript (or proposal for nonfiction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build focused queries for each agent—tight hooks, clear comps, correct guidelines. Use professional one-sheets and targeted pitches for pitch refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow posted submission guidelines and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow all posted guidelines for attachments, formatting, and submission structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read guidelines, personalize each submission, and treat agent time and process with respect—stand out for discipline as much as craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Use clear subject lines: include genre, word count, and agent’s name for quick reference—e.g., Query: [Title] — Mystery — 80,000 words — for [Agent Name].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear subject lines help speed review and make your submission easy to triage among many queries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-agent query policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Only query one Folio agent at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This single-agent rule speeds up review and avoids confusion if declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission tracking and response management
rubrics_metrics.description: Track submission dates, responses, and feedback. Expect replies in weeks or months, not days. Revise and resubmit if an agent gives concrete notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a spreadsheet to note dates, responses, and feedback. Consider feedback with gratitude; move smartly to next agent if declined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrights expertise and active pursuit
rubrics_metrics.description: Agents actively pursue subsidiary rights: film, TV, international, and audio. Subrights teams create complete packages for foreign, audio, and film opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sophisticated timing—simultaneous or staggered subrights sales—can boost attention and income. Co-agents abroad and in-house subrights staff expand global visibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracts protection and specialist scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracts staff safeguard your earnings, policing reversion clauses and subsplits, so your work stays yours when it matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracts specialists closely review clauses like reversion, escalation, and revenue splits. Watch for clear exit/reversion terms and avoid clauses that bind you forever or take future rights without oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career management and long-term strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Career management includes strategic planning for sequels or follow-up titles, full coordination for platform-building and publicity, and long-term revenue by maximizing every possible right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The right agency team means smart strategy, faster feedback, and better deals—plan sequels, manage backlists, and coordinate multi-format launches for sustained earnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfiction platform requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonfiction requests require platform—expertise, credentials, or audience that make a project viable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should demonstrate expertise, credentials, or an existing audience to make nonfiction projects attractive to agents and publishers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children’s/YA suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Folio Jr. specializes in children’s and YA projects, which need pacing, age-appropriate themes, and educational value for extra discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor submissions for school, library, and educational markets; consider pacing and thematic appropriateness for target age groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong comps and bookstore placement clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Expect more interest if your submission includes strong comps, clarity on bookstore placement, commercial hooks for series, or a marketable twist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include comps and explain intended bookstore placement or market segment to signal commercial potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketable hook, series potential, and adaptation readiness
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors with adaptation-ready ideas, series potential, visual storytelling, or standout hooks excel here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects with clear audience, strong comps, and powerful opening chapters win attention; consider whether your idea can extend into series or adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent communication speed and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency excels at fast, clear communication, updating authors throughout submissions, negotiations, and rights deals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear updates replace confusion at every critical stage; authors should expect timely communication about submissions and negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Team structure and in-house expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Senior agents, contracts leads, and subrights staff work in layers, combining boutique attention with serious institutional reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A layered team (senior agent + subrights + contracts) reduces delays in negotiation and allows multiple in-house champions to support a book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid upfront fees; commission-based model
rubrics_metrics.description: Never pay fees up front. Reputable agents are commission-based, earning only if you do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat upfront-fee requests as red flags; legitimate agencies earn through commission from sales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Red flags in agency behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Red flag: agencies dodging questions, lacking public sales records, or pressuring you into instant decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research agent backgrounds, check sales, and walk away from agencies that avoid transparency or apply hard pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware guarantees of success
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t believe every promise. Any agent 'guaranteeing' bestsellers or screen deals is selling hype, not expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Realistic agents discuss strategy and probabilities rather than promising guaranteed outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence, realistic expectations, and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Most breakthroughs come after multiple rejections. Submission volume is high; success comes to those who stand out, follow up professionally, and track their efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect long wait times; be persistent, adapt after feedback, and maintain realistic expectations about time-to-sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responding to Revise & Resubmit (R&R) requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise & Resubmit (R&R) requests signal genuine interest. Take them seriously and act fast, returning a cleaner manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R&R can be a real chance; use agent notes to improve your manuscript and demonstrate responsiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing strategy for subrights sales
rubrics_metrics.description: Sophisticated timing—simultaneous or staggered subrights sales—can boost both attention and income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agents may time foreign, audio, and film submissions to maximize global impact; discuss strategies with subrights teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch refinement and professional materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch refinement ensures your work catches editors’ attention, not just with writing, but with professional one-sheets and targeted pitches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare one-sheets, elevator pitches, and targeted materials to support submissions and subrights efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author participation in marketing and planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors who participate in the marketing and planning process tend to achieve stronger publisher connections and bigger advances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to collaborate on platform-building, publicity, and long-term planning; being engaged helps realize greater success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of backlist management
rubrics_metrics.description: Managing both frontlist launches and literary estates, Folio keeps author rights active, licensed, and earning long after first publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agent who actively manages backlists and estates can generate ongoing revenue and career longevity; view your work as a rights-rich asset.
